fields.h1: Build a Pet Adoption Form for Your Shelter or Rescue
fields.hero_description: Describe how your rescue places animals. Emergent builds the pet adoption form with follow-ups for renters and pet owners, and keeps every application in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Pet Adoption Form Should Ask
fields.features_subheading: Shelter applications share a core set of questions. These six features turn them into a form your adoption team can work from.
fields.feature_1:
The questions shelters already ask

Emergent builds the sections every shelter application shares. Applicants describe their household and their housing, then the pets they have now and the vet who treats them.
fields.feature_2:
Dog and cat questions in one form

Pick a species and the form adjusts. Dog applicants get questions on fencing and daily walks, while cat applicants say whether the new cat will live indoors or go outside.
fields.feature_3:
Applications filed under each animal

Link the form from every adoptable pet's listing, and each application carries that animal's name and ID. Each foster filters the table down to the pets currently in their care.
fields.feature_4:
Status emails at every step

Move an application from received to vet check to approved, and the applicant hears about each change by email. Applicants who are declined get a kind note instead of silence.
fields.feature_5:
Repeat applicants grouped together

Someone who applies for three dogs in a week shows up as one person with three applications. Your team reads the household once and spots a missing vet reference at a glance.
fields.feature_6:
A form on your domain, code in GitHub

Publish the form on the rescue's own domain. Export the full source to GitHub whenever a volunteer developer wants to add a foster portal or a public page of adoptable pets.

fields.usecase_heading: Adoption Forms for Every Kind of Rescue
fields.tab_content_1:
The landlord's okay comes in with the application

Applicants who rent see two extra questions: their landlord's name and phone number, and whether the lease allows a dog over 50 pounds. Homeowners never see them. Every application for Juniper, a shepherd mix, goes straight to her foster, Dana, who works through all 9 in one table and calls the landlords herself.
fields.tab_content_2:
A QR code on every kennel card

A walk-in visitor scans the code at kennel 14 and answers six questions on their phone: who lives at home, other pets, hours away each day. The answers reach the adoption counselor's tablet before the meet. The conversation opens with what the visitor wrote instead of a blank clipboard.
fields.tab_content_3:
No meet-and-greet until the vet calls back

Each application waits at the vet reference step. A volunteer gets the applicant's clinic and phone number, then calls to confirm the two current cats are vaccinated. Once the volunteer marks the reference clear, the applicant gets an email to book a 30-minute meet-and-greet with the foster.
fields.tab_content_4:
Paid and signed before the carrier leaves the table

At the Saturday adoption event, an approved adopter pays the $125 adoption fee through Stripe and signs the contract on the same tablet. Miso's record changes to Adopted, and the contract and receipt go out by email. Nobody keys in paper forms on Monday morning.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Pet Adoption Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what your team does with each answer before you write a question.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Go through the form you use today and mark every question nobody on the team has acted on in the past year. Cut those. What remains is the list you describe to Emergent, and it is usually shorter than expected.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask only what changes a placement, such as housing and the other animals at home. A question about a fenced yard matters for a young husky and means little for a senior cat. Attach questions like that to the animals they fit.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide whether applications go to the foster caring for the animal or to one adoption coordinator. Foster-based rescues usually route by animal. Shelters with a front desk often send everything to whoever is on shift that day.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write a prompt with your questions and say who reviews what. Paste your adoption contract word for word if the form should collect a signature. Emergent builds the form and the applications table, and you change either one by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_5_des: List the steps between submit and approval, such as a landlord call or a home visit, and name the volunteer who owns each one. The application moves forward only when that person marks their step done.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Add the fee and the contract
fields.howto_step_6_des: Set the adoption fee for each species or age group and connect Stripe to collect it. Show the contract and the payment screen only after approval. Adopters your team has not cleared never see either one.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it as a made-up renter
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill the form as a made-up renter with two cats and a dog-friendly lease. Check that the landlord questions appear, the vet step waits for a volunteer and the status emails read well. Then post the link on every animal's listing.
